questions.question: What is the longest prison sentence a traffic law infraction can lead to in Iceland?
questions.explanation: Depending on how serious the infraction is, the punishment ranges from a fine through custody up to three years of imprisonment.

questions.question: A person borrows a car in June and is stopped because it still has studded tires fitted. Who has to pay the fine?
options: The person driving the borrowed car
The registered owner of the car
The insurance company of the car
The workshop that fitted the tires
questions.explanation: The driver answers for the car being in a legal and working condition, even when he is neither the owner nor the registered possessor.

questions.question: When is a drunk person regarded as attempting to operate a vehicle, which the law also forbids?
options: When he walks towards his parked car holding the keys
When he sits in the driving seat with the engine running
When he sits in the passenger seat holding the keys
When he sleeps in the back seat of the parked car
questions.explanation: Article 45 bans the attempt as well as the act, and a driver in place behind a running engine already counts as an attempt.

questions.question: For how long can a drug such as cannabis stay in a person's system?
questions.explanation: Unlike alcohol, which the liver clears within hours, cannabis can remain for weeks, so the impairment and the evidence long outlast the night of use.

questions.question: What is the position of a person who hands alcohol to someone who is about to drive?
options: He commits no offence unless he owns the vehicle
He can be found guilty as an accessory to DUI
He is punished only if an accident follows
He is liable only if the driver is a beginner
questions.explanation: Responsibility does not stop at the driver: supplying the drink, or inviting a drunk person to drive, is itself punishable.

questions.question: Between which blood alcohol levels does the law treat a driver as unable to operate a vehicle safely?
questions.explanation: This band is what the legislator uses to grade the punishment for drunk driving, and it matches 0,25 to 0,60 milligrams of alcohol per litre of exhaled air.

questions.question: A breath test shows more than 0,60 milligrams of alcohol per litre of exhaled air. What follows from that?
options: The driver must be retested with a blood sample
The driver may drive if he feels completely sober
The driver is deemed unfit to operate a vehicle
The driver is given three penalty points
questions.explanation: That reading matches 1,20 promille in the bloodstream, the level above which unfitness to drive is simply presumed rather than assessed.

questions.question: Which of the following actually speeds up the rate at which the liver burns off alcohol?
options: Drinking several cups of strong coffee
Going for a long run in fresh air
Taking a hot bath and then sleeping
Nothing, the burn rate cannot be raised
questions.explanation: The liver works at roughly 20 millilitres of strong liquor per hour whatever you do, which is why alcohol can still be in the blood the next morning.

questions.question: When is a police officer allowed to carry out an alcohol test on a driver?
options: Only when the driver smells clearly of alcohol
Only when a court has issued a written warrant
During a routine check or after a traffic accident
Only when an accident has caused personal injury
questions.explanation: No prior suspicion is required for the test, and the driver is obliged to comply with the officer's request.

questions.question: How much more likely is a very sleepy driver to have a traffic accident than a fresh one?
questions.explanation: Tiredness lengthens reaction time and narrows peripheral vision, so the risk multiplies well before the driver actually falls asleep.

questions.question: A driver becomes very sleepy on a journey. How long a nap is already worth taking?
questions.explanation: Research shows a short stop of about a quarter of an hour in a safe parking spot restores enough alertness to be worthwhile.

questions.question: How many penalty points does using a mobile phone without hands-free equipment carry?
questions.explanation: It sits in the lowest band, together with an unfastened seat belt and driving the wrong way in a one-way street.

questions.question: A medication box carries a red triangle on its label. What does that require of the person taking it?
options: He must halve the dose on days he drives
He must wait 24 hours after the last dose
He must consult a doctor before he drives
He must keep the prescription in the car
questions.explanation: The triangle marks side effects such as sleepiness, longer reaction time or reduced eyesight, so only a doctor can judge whether driving is safe.

questions.question: What is the highest fine that can be imposed for breaking the traffic law?
questions.explanation: 240 thousand is only the quoted example for a repeated DUI offence; the ceiling set for traffic fines is higher than that.

questions.question: What does a driver gain by paying his fine within 30 days of the date of issue?
options: A discount of 25% off the original amount
A discount of 50% off the original amount
The cancellation of any penalty points given
The removal of the entry from his record
questions.explanation: The discount only reduces the money owed; penalty points and the record of the infringement are unaffected by prompt payment.

questions.question: How does the penalty point system treat a driver who is caught driving under the influence?
options: He is given three points and a formal warning
He is given twelve points in one go
He is given no points but loses his license
He is given points only from the second offence
questions.explanation: The heavy fine together with the revocation is regarded as punishment enough, so DUI is kept outside the points system entirely.

questions.question: How many penalty points does a driver receive for crossing a junction on a red light?
questions.explanation: It falls in the middle band, alongside ignoring a stop sign, failing to give way under the right-hand rule and disobeying a police officer.

questions.question: How many accumulated penalty points cost the holder of a full driving license his license?
questions.explanation: Points are erased three years after they are given, so the total has to build up inside that window before revocation follows.

questions.question: A driver has reached the point limit and loses his license. How long does that revocation last?
questions.explanation: Once the period is over the points that caused it are wiped immediately, so the driver can collect his license and start again with a clean slate.

questions.question: A driver has been sentenced to lifetime revocation of his license. When may he apply for a new one?
questions.explanation: Lifetime means lifetime, but an application is allowed after five years, and an approved applicant must sit both the theory and the practical exam again.

questions.question: On a road where the limit is 30 km/h, exceeding it by more than 26 km/h carries how many points?
questions.explanation: Gross speeding sits in the top band, the same as exceeding a 50 to 60 km/h limit by more than 36 km/h.

questions.question: How many penalty points cost the holder of a temporary driving license his license?
questions.explanation: Rookie drivers are held to a far stricter limit than experienced ones, and getting the license back requires a special course and both exams again.

questions.question: What must the holder of a temporary driving license achieve before a permanent one can be issued?
options: Twelve months of driving with an instructor present
Two years without receiving any traffic fine
Three years without causing a traffic accident
Twelve months in a row with no penalty points
questions.explanation: A single penalty point during the qualifying period restarts the wait, and the driver must also pass a driving assessment before the permanent license is issued.
